title: Citation resolution and quote verification
summary: Checking that every citation points at a real passage and that every quoted span actually appears in it.
what: Two mechanical checks after generation: does the cited chunk id exist in the index for this run, and does the quoted text appear verbatim in that chunk.
why: Models invent citations. They also paraphrase a quotation while presenting it as verbatim. Both are checkable without a model, and both should fail the response rather than reach a reader.
how: Citation resolution is a lookup. Quote verification is string containment first, with a model judge only where containment fails — because a legitimate quote can differ by whitespace or an ellipsis.
in_this_project: Planned for Phase 2 as part of the generation graph. Citation accuracy and citation coverage are defined in the metric content and reported separately: accuracy asks whether citations point at supporting passages, coverage asks whether factual claims carry a citation at all. A system can score well on one and badly on the other.

advantages: Deterministic and cheap for the common case
No model needed for the containment check
limitations: Cannot tell whether a resolved citation actually supports the claim without a judge

pitfalls: Checking the citation resolves but not that it supports the claim
Measuring accuracy without coverage, so a system citing almost nothing scores well

use: Any system whose answers are acted on
